confirmed_findings: Patient Agreements boilerplate must not enter next_steps.
Problem titles and clinical fragments must be routed by meaning rather than sent to one default bucket.
Plain newlines must split adjacent ROS/history entries.
HPI demographic introductions and diagnosed-with phrasing must supplement dedicated history sections.
Abbreviated colon headers caused the D2N069 empty-field failure.
Standalone Medical, Surgical, and PAST SURGICAL HISTORY labels are headings, not history content.
Mr., Mrs., Ms., and Dr. must not be treated as sentence boundaries.
Short clinical denials such as Denies vomiting and Denies hematuria must be retained.
Positive HPI infection and lingering-cold descriptions must supplement a non-empty ROS section.
owner_feedback.approval_note: The v3 corrections are owner-requested and implemented for review. The overall extraction spec remains draft until Chloe reviews the regenerated eight-case sample.

supersedes: earlier draft that assumed a fixed 4-section template (HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS / PHYSICAL EXAM / RESULTS / ASSESSMENT AND PLAN) based on a secondary paper description. That template is only one of many; real notes vary a lot. This version is built and spot-checked directly against the uploaded aci-bench-2023.zip.
source_dataset: ACI-Bench (challenge_data split, from the uploaded aci-bench-corpus)
source_dataset_version: Confirmed row counts match the published splits exactly: train.csv = 67, valid.csv = 20, clinicalnlp_taskB_test1.csv = 40, clinicalnlp_taskC_test2.csv = 40, clef_taskC_test3.csv = 40.

source_files_confirmed.note: 'dataset' here is a sub-source label with three values: aci, virtassist, virtscribe - these are three originally separate note-writing conventions merged into one corpus. 'encounter_id' (e.g. D2N001) is the join key between the note/dialogue file and its metadata file, and is what we should use as source_field. 'id' is a different, sub-source-internal identifier (e.g. VA049) - don't use this as the primary key. 'cc' is a short chief-complaint string and '2nd_complaints' is a semicolon-separated list of secondary conditions - both useful as cross-check signal, not primary extraction sources.

note_structure_finding: There is no fixed section template. Across train+valid+test1+test2+test3, 30 distinct literal ALL-CAPS-standalone-line header strings appear (e.g. 'CHIEF COMPLAINT'), and even within a single sub-source (e.g. 'aci') different notes use different subsets of headers. Extraction has to work off a header-alias table, not a fixed split. IMPORTANT CORRECTION (found while investigating the D2N069 empty-fields bug): 16 of 207 notes (7.7%, spanning both 'virtassist' and 'aci' sub-sources) use a SECOND, entirely different header format - abbreviated headers with a trailing colon on their own line (e.g. 'CC:', 'HPI:', 'MSK:', 'RESPIRATORY:', 'OTC:') instead of full-caps standalone lines. The original header survey's regex only matched the full-caps style and completely missed this format - these 16 notes were silently mis-surveyed as having few/no sections, when they actually have normal structure just written in abbreviated form. D2N069 (the empty-symptoms case flagged for review) is one of these 16: it has a normal HPI: section with clear symptom content, but the extraction never saw it because the header-detection regex doesn't recognize 'HPI:' as a header at all.

abbreviated_header_alias_table.status: syntax inventory verified across all 207 notes: 16 notes use this format and the five aliases below are the complete set matched by the stated pattern; semantic routing remains subject to extraction regression tests
abbreviated_header_alias_table.detection_pattern: Use ^([A-Z]{2,20}):\s*$ multiline to inventory this style. Only known top-level aliases CC/HPI open new scored sections. MSK/RESPIRATORY/OTC inherit their current parent section so nested exam/result labels are not promoted into the wrong gold bucket.
abbreviated_header_alias_table.CC:: symptoms_bucket (same as CHIEF COMPLAINT; chief complaints are current symptoms, not patient history)
abbreviated_header_alias_table.HPI:: symptoms_bucket (same as HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS)
abbreviated_header_alias_table.MSK:: nested under PHYSICAL EXAM in all 4 occurrences; inherit the ignored exam bucket rather than opening a symptoms section
abbreviated_header_alias_table.RESPIRATORY:: nested under PHYSICAL EXAM in its only occurrence; inherit the ignored exam bucket rather than opening a symptoms section
abbreviated_header_alias_table.OTC:: nested under RESULTS in its only occurrence; do not assume this means over-the-counter medication or route it to history
abbreviated_header_alias_table.corpus_inventory: Across all 207 notes, the pattern finds exactly CC (10 notes), HPI (10), MSK (4), RESPIRATORY (1), and OTC (1), spanning 16 distinct notes. Only CC/HPI are top-level abbreviated aliases. MSK/RESPIRATORY/OTC are nested labels whose parent section controls routing.

symptoms.primary_source: CHIEF COMPLAINT/CC plus all REVIEW OF SYSTEMS/REVIEW OF SYMPTOMS entries. Chief complaints belong in symptoms, not history.
symptoms.supplemental_source: Always scan HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS and merge keyword-matched symptom sentences even when ROS is non-empty. This includes pain/onset/severity language and generalized illness descriptions such as frequent infections or lingering colds.
symptoms.fallback: If dedicated symptom sections are absent, the same HPI keyword extraction becomes the primary source rather than a separate rule.
symptoms.confidence: medium-high for the ROS-bullet case (very clean), medium for the HPI-narrative fallback case

history.primary_source: All history_bucket sections present in the note (MEDICAL/PAST/SOCIAL/FAMILY/SURGICAL HISTORY, MEDICATIONS, ALLERGIES, etc.). CHIEF COMPLAINT is excluded from history.
history.supplemental_source: Always scan HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS, even when dedicated history sections already produced items. Merge and deduplicate sentences containing 'history of', 'history significant for', 'medical history significant for', 'previously', 'prior', 'PMH', 'diagnosed with', or an age/sex demographic introduction that names established conditions before 'who presents'.
history.confirmed_bug: Direct review of D2N068 showed that a recurring demographic-introduction sentence names established conditions using 'medical history significant for' rather than the old trigger 'history of'. The extractor therefore missed those conditions. Fix: always supplement dedicated history sections from HPI and support 'medical history significant for', 'history significant for', 'diagnosed with', and the recurring age/sex/condition introduction pattern.
history.confidence: high when dedicated history sections exist, medium on the narrative fallback (lower until the keyword gap above is fixed)

risks.primary_source_combined_assessment_and_p: When the note has a single 'ASSESSMENT AND PLAN' section (93 occurrences corpus-wide; verified 41/42 sampled instances use labeled sub-bullets per numbered problem), take only the 'Medical Reasoning:' labeled sub-bullet under each numbered problem as a risks entry.
risks.primary_source_separate_assessment: When the note has a separate 'ASSESSMENT' section (38 occurrences corpus-wide, mostly the virtscribe sub-source), this section is typically already a clean bullet list of diagnosis names with no further reasoning text - take each bullet line directly as a risks entry.
risks.secondary_source: RESULTS section: take sentences describing an abnormal finding (containing 'elevated', 'abnormal', 'positive', 'low', 'high' next to a lab/vital value) as additional risks entries.
risks.fallback: In the rare case (~2%, roughly 1 in 42 sampled) where a combined ASSESSMENT AND PLAN section has no labeled sub-bullets, fall back to keyword rule: sentences containing 'differential', 'rule out', 'concern for', 'risk of', 'possible', or a diagnosis name.
risks.confidence: high for the labeled-sub-bullet case and the separate-ASSESSMENT-bullet-list case (both verified against real data), medium-low for the unlabeled fallback case

next_steps.primary_source_combined_assessment_and_p: Within the same 'ASSESSMENT AND PLAN' section, take the 'Medical Treatment:', 'Additional Testing:', and 'Patient Education and Counseling:' labeled sub-bullets under each numbered problem as next_steps entries.
next_steps.primary_source_separate_plan: When the note has a separate 'PLAN' section, it's free-form prose grouped by diagnosis heading - take each per-diagnosis paragraph as one next_steps entry (split into individual sentences only if the paragraph is unusually long, e.g. over ~60 words).
next_steps.secondary_source: INSTRUCTIONS, PROCEDURE, and ORDERS sections when present - each becomes a next_steps entry.
next_steps.fallback: Same action-verb keyword rule as before ('will order', 'start', 'refer', 'follow up', 'schedule', 'recommend', 'continue', etc.) for the rare unlabeled combined-section case.
next_steps.confidence: high for the labeled-sub-bullet and separate-PLAN cases, medium-high on INSTRUCTIONS/PROCEDURE/ORDERS, medium on the keyword fallback

sections_not_mapped_to_gold: exam_vitals_bucket (PHYSICAL EXAM/EXAMINATION, EXAM, VITALS, VITALS REVIEWED) is kept as background context only, not scored against any of the four output fields.
sentence_splitting_rule: Split section text on bullet markers, numbered lists, plain newlines, and sentence-ending punctuation, while protecting the common honorifics Mr., Mrs., Ms., and Dr. from sentence-boundary detection. Discard fragments shorter than 3 words except dedicated history/problem-title entries and short clinical statements beginning with Denies, Reports, Endorses, Positive for, or Negative for. Direct review of D2N085 confirmed that adjacent newline-separated ROS systems can lack terminal punctuation, so newline splitting is mandatory rather than a fallback.
empty_section_handling: If a bucket has no matching section in a given note, the corresponding output array is empty, not omitted - matches the existing schema rule that empty arrays are allowed for H4.

boilerplate_stoplist.status: confirmed high-prevalence issue, not a rare edge case
boilerplate_stoplist.finding: A fixed template line beginning with 'Patient Agreements:' appears in 97 of 207 notes (46.9%), in the aci and virtassist sub-sources. It was leaking into next_steps in every reviewed sample that contained it (H4-001, H4-002, H4-008).
boilerplate_stoplist.fix: Drop this exact sentence (and likely a small number of near-identical template variants - worth grep-ing for 'Patient Agreements:' as a prefix generally) before bucketing next_steps content. Given how common this is, this single fix alone would clean up nearly half the corpus's next_steps output.

numbered_problem_title_handling.status: confirmed gap in the original rule, found while checking H4-001/D2N084
numbered_problem_title_handling.finding: In the combined ASSESSMENT AND PLAN format, a short problem title may be numbered or unnumbered and is followed by labeled reasoning/treatment/testing/counseling bullets. The original parser did not terminate the prior labeled block at a new title, so titles leaked into next_steps.
numbered_problem_title_handling.fix: Terminate each labeled sub-bullet at the next numbered problem title so the title cannot leak into next_steps. Route the title by meaning: symptom/problem descriptions such as pain go to symptoms; 'history of'/'status post' titles go to history; diagnoses and clinical findings such as a murmur go to risks. Deduplicate a routed title against items already extracted from other sections.

secondary_history_header_handling.finding: Standalone Medical and Surgical subheadings and the PAST SURGICAL HISTORY heading leaked into history as independent entries in H4-REVIEW-003, H4-REVIEW-005, and H4-REVIEW-006.
secondary_history_header_handling.fix: Recognize these labels as history section headers. Preserve their following clinical content but never emit the header text itself. Drop context-free missing-value placeholders such as None reported rather than presenting them as clinical history.

honorific_sentence_splitting.finding: Mr., Ms., and Dr. were mistaken for sentence-ending punctuation in H4-REVIEW-005 and H4-REVIEW-006, causing the beginning of sentences to be discarded.
honorific_sentence_splitting.fix: Protect periods in Mr., Mrs., Ms., and Dr. before sentence splitting and restore them afterward.

short_clinical_statement_handling.finding: Two-word denials following another sentence, including Denies vomiting and Denies hematuria, were removed by the three-word fragment floor in H4-REVIEW-004.
short_clinical_statement_handling.fix: Retain short fragments that begin with an explicit clinical assertion or denial while continuing to filter non-content fragments.

unmapped_policy_notes: A note whose header set doesn't match any bucket in the alias table above for an entire required area (e.g. no chief_complaint, symptoms, history, assessment, or plan bucket found anywhere) should be flagged for manual review rather than silently producing all-empty output, since that likely means an unrecognized header string was used and the alias table needs another entry added.
known_limitations: The header alias table was built from a real, but not exhaustive, header survey across all five ACI-Bench splits (30 distinct header strings found). If the actual conversion turns up a header string not in this table, that's a sign the table needs another entry, not a bug in the note.

The 'Medical Reasoning: / Medical Treatment: / Additional Testing: / Patient Education and Counseling:' sub-bullet split for combined ASSESSMENT AND PLAN sections has now been checked across the full 207-encounter corpus (all five splits), not just a sample: 91 of 93 occurrences (97.8%) use the labeled sub-bullet format, consistent with the earlier train+valid spot-check (97.6%). This is now a confirmed rule, not a sampled estimate.

Rare one-off headers (HIV, BIRTH HISTORY, EKG) appear only once or twice in the whole corpus and were bucketed by best guess rather than by seeing enough examples to be confident - low stakes given how rare they are, but worth a manual glance if they show up in the sampled pilot cases.

MTS-Dialog (the supplementary source mentioned in the earlier proposal) has NOT been inspected yet the way ACI-Bench just was - its section-header conventions are known to be looser, so this alias table should not be assumed to transfer directly. Needs its own inspection pass before use.

split_mapping.decision: Use ACI-Bench's own splits as-is, re-labeled to our metadata.split enum. Do not use MTS-Dialog at all - ACI-Bench alone (207 encounters) covers the pilot's needs.
split_mapping.sub_source_balance_check: Confirmed all three sub-sources (aci/virtassist/virtscribe) appear in roughly the same proportion in every split (aci ~50-55%, virtassist ~25%, virtscribe ~20%), including the small 20-case valid split (11/5/4). No extra stratified sampling needed - the natural composition already covers all three note-writing styles.

mapping.train.csv (n=67): development - used to build and debug the extraction rule
mapping.valid.csv (n=20): pilot - this is what tomorrow's pilot run uses
mapping.clinicalnlp_taskB_test1.csv (n=40): validation - used once the rule is stable, to check it generalizes
mapping.clinicalnlp_taskC_test2.csv (n=40) + cle: test - locked, held out until the main benchmark stage, nobody tunes the rule against these 80

difficulty_generation_rule.status: draft - thresholds computed directly from the actual 207-encounter corpus (all five splits), not estimated

measured_distribution.numbered_problem_lists_note: Only meaningful for the 'aci' sub-source style (61 of ~112 aci-style notes use numbered problem lists like '1. Right knee pain.'; virtassist/virtscribe almost never do - 2 and 1 occurrences respectively). Treated as a bonus hard-signal only, not a primary rule, since it isn't comparable across sub-sources.

difficulty_generation_rule.medium: Everything that is neither easy nor hard by the rules below.
difficulty_generation_rule.hard: distinct_section_headers >= 10, OR dialogue_char_length > 7532, OR (aci-style note) numbered problem count >= 3.
difficulty_generation_rule.rationale: More section headers means more distinct clinical topics the agent has to extract correctly across all four output fields at once. Longer dialogue means more raw material to condense and a higher chance of missing something. Three or more numbered problems (when the note style makes that countable) means real multi-morbidity, which is harder to keep straight across symptoms/history/risks/next_steps than a single-problem visit.
